q: What does the portable Linux folder change on my computer when it first starts?
a: Only your user folder: the first time it starts, the portable `.tar.gz` adds its own app-menu entry and Revolution's icon there (rounded macOS style by default, or Square if you picked that under Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ **App icon**). It does it again after you move the folder or update, never writes over a packaged entry or a launcher you made, and `FILMCRAFT_NO_DESKTOP_ENTRY=1` stops it. Nothing system-wide is installed; deleting the folder removes Revolution (projects, settings and caches stay in your data folder).

q: I'd rather manage my own launchers. Can I start the tarball build without it touching my app menu?
a: Yes. Start it with `FILMCRAFT_NO_DESKTOP_ENTRY=1` set, for example make your launcher's command `env FILMCRAFT_NO_DESKTOP_ENTRY=1 ~/Apps/revolution/latest/revolution`. You may not even need it: Revolution never writes over a launcher you made yourself (or a packaged entry). Trade-off: with the variable set, keeping the menu entry pointing at the right folder after you move or update is your job.

q: Set up the portable Linux build with a square icon in the app menu.
a:
1. Unpack it into its own folder: `mkdir -p ~/Apps/revolution && tar -xzf revolution-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz -C ~/Apps/revolution`.
2. Point the `latest` link at it: `ln -sfn revolution-<version> ~/Apps/revolution/latest` (this also lets it update itself).
3. Start `~/Apps/revolution/latest/revolution` once: it adds its app-menu entry and the rounded icon to your user folder.
4. Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ **Appearance…**: set **App icon** to **Square** (agents: `appearance.appIcon` = `square`).

The window icon changes at once; if your desktop caches icons, the menu and taskbar icon change after you log out and back in.

q: Do the AppImage and the Flatpak add themselves to the app menu the way the tarball does?
a: Not in the same way. The .deb, .rpm and Flatpak are installed by your package manager, rounded icon included. The AppImage carries the icon, but your desktop menu doesn't list it unless you add it yourself or use a helper such as AppImageLauncher or Gear Lever. Adding its own entry on first start is what the portable `.tar.gz` does, because it has no installer.
